bib.title: SkillsBench: Benchmarking How Well Agent Skills Work Across Diverse Tasks
authors: and about 60 more, last author Dawn Song

question: How much do curated Agent Skills (structured procedural packages) improve LLM agent task success, and when do they fail?
hypothesis: Curated Skills improve agent pass rates, but unevenly across model-harness stacks, domains and Skill designs (stated as findings; no formal hypothesis statement).
contributions: Narrow: a quantitative answer to how much Skills help: 33.9% to 50.5% (+16.6 pp) across 18 model-harness configurations on 87 tasks
Broad: a paired with/without evaluation framework with contributor-driven sourcing, leakage-controlled task-to-Skill decoupling and the BenchFlow containerized harness
Open-sourced benchmark, harness and public trajectories/results

method.summary: 87 containerized tasks across 8 domains, each with human-written instruction, expert-authored Skills bundle, oracle and deterministic pytest verifier, run on BenchFlow under no-Skills and curated-Skills conditions (plus a self-generated diagnostic on 3 configs) for 18 model-harness configurations, 3 trials each. Skill efficacy is the paired difference in task-macro pass rate and Hake normalized gain.
method.task: agentic terminal tasks in 8 expertise-heavy domains; measure of augmentation efficacy (paired with vs without Skills)

datasets.name: SkillsBench
datasets.size: 87 tasks (6 Core <60 min, 53 Extended 1-4 h, 28 Extreme >4 h); domains: Software Engineering 16, Industrial & Physical Systems 14, Natural Science 14, Office & White Collar 14, Finance & Economics 9, Mathematics & OR 8, Cybersecurity 7, Media & Content Production 5
datasets.source: 400 candidate submissions from 142 contributors, filtered by automated gates and human review (22% acceptance); open-sourced
datasets.preprocessing: gates: structure, oracle must pass 100%, instruction provenance (GPTZero plus human label), Skill-to-solution leakage audit via Claude Code Agent SDK validation agent; tasks with no separation between conditions rejected as low-signal; 85 of 87 verifiers use pytest with CTRF

datasets.name: Skill ecosystem snapshot
datasets.split: used only for ecosystem analysis and Skill selection
datasets.preprocessing: deduplicated within each source, then summed

models.name: 18 model-harness configs: OpenHands with GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4 Mini, Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Opus 4.7, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Gemini 3.5 Flash, Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite, GLM 5.1, Kimi K2.6, DeepSeek V4 Pro, DeepSeek V4 Flash, Grok 4.3, MiniMax M3, MiniMax M2.7; Gemini CLI + Gemini 3.1 Pro; Claude Code + Opus 4.7; Codex CLI + GPT-5.5

other.harness_versions: Table 7 column says only the harness name; no version numbers found in the text

models.name: Anthropic skill-creator
models.architecture: a Skill used by the agent to author skill packs

inference.decoding: temperature 0 (stated deterministic sampling) for all models
inference.samples: 3 selected public trials per (configuration, task, condition) cell; 87 x 3 frame; 9,396 slots (18 configs x 87 tasks x 2 conditions x 3 trials); self-generated: 258, 258, 253 of 261 slots
inference.prompting: no-Skills: task instruction only. Curated: full environment/skills/ directory exposed before the instruction through each harness's native loading mechanism; instruction never names Skills. Reasoning effort: highest available per model. Claude Code self-gen used effort max vs high for baseline; Codex xhigh.

parameters.context_management: sliding window with 8K token limit, oldest turns dropped (App D.9; implausibly small given 1M+ tokens per trial in Table 15, so verify against the release)
parameters.container: ubuntu:24.04, 1-4 CPUs, 2-10 GB memory, 10 GB storage, no GPU, deleted after each trial
parameters.retry: unscored, stale or rate-limited runs audited and rerun; timeouts scored as failures only when no healthy replacement exists

other.context_budget_note: App A.4 says median Skill size (~1.8k tokens) informed an 8K context budget allocation

metrics.name: task-macro pass rate
metrics.definition: per-task verifier reward averaged over the 3 trials, then averaged over 87 tasks (Terminal-Bench style)

metrics.name: normalized gain g
metrics.definition: (pass_skill - pass_vanilla)/(1 - pass_vanilla) (Hake 1998); mean row macro-averages per-config g

metrics.name: Skill Invocation Rate
metrics.definition: share of curated-Skills trials whose trajectory reads or invokes a task-bundled Skill

eval.protocol: paired at (configuration, task) level; 95% binomial Wald CIs 1.96*sqrt(p(1-p)/n) with n = selected result-file count per cell (261), which treats trials as independent and ignores task pairing; no significance test; normalized gain is a point estimate. Deterministic pytest verifier, no LLM judge.

availability.code: open-sourced benchmark, BenchFlow harness (github.com/benchflow-ai/benchflow); also on AgentBeats
availability.data: public trajectories/results released (HF main + PR#11 mentioned)

prompts.text: Use the skill-creator skill exactly as provided. Read /instruction.md and inspect the task environment only as needed to understand the reusable workflow. Do not solve the task directly. Create one or more complete Anthropic-standard skill packs as immediate child directories under: /app/generated-skills Use this suggested path if one skill is enough: /app/generated-skills/<task>-skill Each generated skill pack path must look like /app/generated-skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md. It may include scripts/, references/, assets/, examples, or other bundled resources when they help a fresh solver avoid repeated work. The solver context will start with a clean agent session and only the generated skill packs mounted. Make the skills useful for solving this task type from the same sandbox environment.

results.claim: Curated Skills raise mean pass rate across 18 configurations
results.setup: 87 tasks, 8 domains, 18 model-harness configs, no-Skills vs curated Skills, 3 trials per cell (9,396 trials), temperature 0, deterministic pytest verifier, task-macro pass rate
results.quote: Curated Skills raise the average pass rate from 33.9% to 50.5% (+16.6 percentage points; 25.5% normalized gain), with configuration-level gains ranging from +4.1 to +25.7 pp.

results.claim: Mean normalized gain across configurations
results.setup: 87 tasks, 8 domains, 18 model-harness configs, no-Skills vs curated Skills, 3 trials per cell (9,396 trials), temperature 0, deterministic pytest verifier, task-macro pass rate; g macro-averaged per configuration, not recomputed from mean pass rates
results.quote: Curated Skills raise the average pass rate from 33.9% to 50.5% (+16.6 percentage points; 25.5% normalized gain)

results.quote: The highest with-Skills pass rates are OpenHands + GPT-5.5 (67.3%), Codex + GPT-5.5 (66.5%), and Claude Code + Opus 4.7 (61.2%).

limits: Terminal-based containerized tasks only; may not transfer to GUI agents, multi-agent coordination or very long-horizon workflows (Section 6.1).
Skills injection adds context, so gains may partly be 'more context'; no length-matched baseline (random or irrelevant text, retrieval-only docs) was run (Section 6.1).

Self-generated deficit mixes content quality with discovery and creator/solver interference; Claude Code realization shares sandbox state and used higher effort; Codex/Gemini packs generated once and reused; audit of only 12 trajectories chosen for extreme gaps; one verifier (3d-scan-calc) was patched ten days after the runs.
Benchmark Skills come from the top quality quartile (mean 10.1/12 vs ecosystem 6.2/12) so results are an optimistic scenario; Skill-task matching is curated, not automatic.

Skill-count and Skill-length ablations are observational splits over different task subsets (baselines differ, e.g. Standard bucket no-Skills 19.8% vs ~38% elsewhere; Comprehensive N=5), not controlled experiments.
Cybersecurity (N=7) and Media (N=5) domain slices are descriptive only per the authors; per-domain N ranges 5 to 16.
Containerization does not give perfect determinism or immunity to training-set leakage; temperature 0 does not remove nondeterminism.
Claude models are trained with awareness of the Agent Skills spec, which may advantage them; 16 of 18 configs use OpenHands so the harness comparison rests on 3 model families.
CIs use a Wald binomial on 261 trials per cell, treating trials as independent; no paired test is reported despite the paired design.
Results are on fast-moving, preview-labelled model snapshots and harness versions; integration of Skills in harnesses can change.
